cards.text: Elijah the Tishbite is the man who told Ahab, king of Israel, there'd be no dew or rain except at his word (1 Kings 16:29; 17:1). Now, after a long time, in the third year of the drought, the word of the LORD comes to Elijah again.

cards.question: Three years into the drought, what does the LORD tell Elijah to do?

answers.text: Go and present himself to Ahab
Hide again by the Brook of Cherith
Stay on with the widow in Zarephath

cards.question: Along with sending Elijah to Ahab, the LORD makes a promise. He will send ___ upon the face of the earth.

cards.text: So Elijah heads out to face the king. Meanwhile, the famine is severe in Samaria.
And Ahab summons Obadiah, the man in charge of the palace. Remember that name, friend.

cards.question: Obadiah, the man in charge of Ahab's palace, greatly fears the LORD.

cards.text: When Jezebel, Ahab's wife, slaughtered the prophets of the LORD, Obadiah took a hundred of them and hid them (1 Kings 16:31). A HUNDRED prophets, friend, and I can't hide ONE cookie in my bakery without leaving a crumb trail.

cards.question: How did Obadiah hide those hundred prophets of the LORD?

cards.text: Now Ahab gives Obadiah a job. Go throughout the land, to every spring and every valley.

cards.question: What is Ahab hoping to find at every spring and valley?

answers.text: Grass to keep the horses and mules alive
Grain to feed the hungry people of Samaria
Water to fill up the palace wells again

cards.text: So they divide the land to explore, and the hunt is on for one patch of green. I know that feeling, friend. That's me every time a chocolate chip rolls under the oven.

cards.question: Once Ahab and Obadiah divide up the land, how do they search it?

answers.text: Each goes his own way by himself
Together with a band of soldiers
Through servants sent from the palace

cards.text: Obadiah's out there on his own, checking springs and valleys. And SUDDENLY, there's Elijah, right in front of him.

cards.question: When Obadiah recognizes Elijah, he falls facedown.

cards.text: Obadiah asks, "Is it you, my lord Elijah?" Elijah's answer is simple: "It is I," he says, calm as a cookie cooling on the rack.

cards.question: What does Elijah tell Obadiah to do next?

answers.text: Go tell Ahab that Elijah is here
Gather the hidden prophets of the LORD
Keep Elijah hidden from King Ahab

cards.text: Friend, I bet Obadiah's stomach just dropped straight into his sandals. This man does NOT like that plan.

cards.question: What does Obadiah think Ahab will do to him if he delivers Elijah's message?

answers.text: Throw him out of the palace
Send him off to search more

cards.text: Obadiah explains: there's no nation or kingdom where Ahab hasn't sent someone to search for Elijah. Friend, I sat in a junk drawer for YEARS and nobody checked one cabinet for me.

cards.question: When a kingdom told Ahab's searchers that Elijah wasn't there, Ahab made that kingdom swear they hadn't found him.

cards.text: And NOW Elijah wants him to walk up to that king and say "Elijah is here!" Obadiah's got another worry, too.

cards.question: What does Obadiah worry will happen to Elijah once Obadiah leaves him?

answers.text: The Spirit of the LORD will carry him off
Ahab's searchers will catch up to him first
He will slip back into hiding by the brook

cards.text: Obadiah says if he tells Ahab and the king doesn't find Elijah, Ahab will kill him. Then Obadiah reads Elijah his whole résumé, feared the LORD from his youth, hid a hundred prophets, and closes with "He will kill me!"

cards.question: Elijah swears by the LORD of Hosts that he will present himself to Ahab ___.

cards.text: So Obadiah goes and tells Ahab, and Ahab goes to meet Elijah. Every nation, every kingdom, and the big search ends with one guy walking back in going "Uh, boss?"
Ahab sees Elijah and skips the hello. He says, "Is that you, O troubler of Israel?"

cards.question: Ahab calls Elijah the troubler of Israel. Who does Elijah say has really troubled Israel?
Why does Elijah say Ahab and his father's house have troubled Israel?

answers.text: They left the LORD's commandments to follow the Baals
They kept taxing the people all through the famine
They sold Israel's land off to foreign kings

cards.text: Then the man the king's been hunting everywhere starts giving the KING orders. Summon all Israel, Elijah says.

cards.question: Where does Elijah tell Ahab to summon all Israel to meet him?
Besides all Israel, who else does Elijah want Ahab to bring to Mount Carmel?

answers.text: The prophets of Baal and Asherah
The elders and officials of Samaria

cards.text: He wants the four hundred and fifty prophets of Baal and the four hundred prophets of Asherah who eat at Jezebel's table, plus ONE Elijah. Pull up a chair, friend, because this story is NOT done.

findings.problem: This story card is three sentences: 'So they divide the land to explore, and the hunt is on for one patch of green.' / 'I know that feeling, friend.' / 'That's me every time a chocolate chip rolls under the oven.'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: No card ever tells that Obadiah provided the hidden prophets with food and water. The text says it in 18:4 and again in 18:13, in the middle of a severe famine. Card 7 and stop 2 card 11 both leave it out, so the baker misses how Obadiah kept the prophets alive.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: 'calm as a cookie cooling on the rack' states a feeling as fact. The text says only that Elijah answered 'It is I.' It never says he was calm, and the line isn't marked as Papa Dorin's guess.

rule.text: Feelings: He can guess at a feeling, marked as his own ("I think," "I bet"). Never as fact.

findings.problem: This story card packs in more than two beats: Obadiah's fear that Ahab will kill him if Elijah vanishes (18:12), his record of fearing the LORD and hiding a hundred prophets (18:12-13), and his closing 'He will kill me!' (18:14).

rule.text: Aim for one beat per story card. Two is the most. If a story card has more than two things happening, split it.

findings.problem: The right answer, 'They left the LORD's commandments to follow the Baals,' is the only one with biblical wording. The wrong answers, 'They kept taxing the people all through the famine' and 'They sold Israel's land off to foreign kings,' sound modern and economic or political, so the right answer stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: Multiple choice dominates the stop: 7 of its 10 choice cards are multiple choice, with only 2 true or false and 1 fill in the blank.

rule.text: Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern. No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.
